title: WhatsApp forward claims RBI is recalling all ₹500 notes by December
claim: RBI has announced that all ₹500 notes will be recalled from circulation by December 2026 and must be deposited in banks immediately.
content:
URGENT!! RBI OFFICIAL NOTICE: All ₹500 notes will be BANNED from December 1, 2026. Deposit all your cash in bank IMMEDIATELY or it will become WORTHLESS. Forward to all family members!!!

— Forwarded many times

comments.content: I checked the RBI website and there is no such announcement. This looks like a repeat of the 2016 demonetization rumour.
My grandmother received this and was panicking. Thank you for checking.

evidence.title: No RBI press release found
evidence.description: Searched RBI official website (rbi.org.in) press releases from October 2026. No announcement regarding ₹500 note recall exists.

title: Message claims free government laptop scheme for students
claim: The central government is giving free laptops to all students who fill an online form and pay ₹299 registration fee.
content: 🎓 FREE LAPTOP from Government of India! All students (Class 8 to College) can get a FREE laptop. Just fill the form at gov-laptop-free.in and pay ₹299 registration fee. Limited time offer! Forward to all student groups!

comments.content: The website 'gov-laptop-free.in' is not a government domain. Government websites use .gov.in or .nic.in domains.

evidence.title: Fake domain — not a government website
evidence.description: The domain 'gov-laptop-free.in' is not registered under the .gov.in or .nic.in TLD used by official government websites. This appears to be a phishing site designed to collect personal information and payment.

title: Audio clip claims UIDAI is deactivating Aadhaar cards not linked to mobile
claim: UIDAI will deactivate all Aadhaar cards not linked to a mobile number by October 31, 2026.
content:
🚨 URGENT AADHAAR ALERT 🚨
UIDAI will DEACTIVATE your Aadhaar if your mobile number is not linked by October 31. You will not be able to use any government services. Link it now at the nearest centre!

— Forwarded multiple times

comments.content: UIDAI has repeatedly clarified that Aadhaar cards cannot be deactivated for not linking a mobile number. Mobile linking is optional and for the convenience of the holder.

evidence.title: UIDAI official clarification on X (Twitter)
evidence.description: UIDAI's verified X account has posted multiple clarifications stating that Aadhaar is never deactivated for not linking a mobile number.

title: Claim: Eating ice cream after fish causes skin disease
claim: Eating ice cream within 2 hours of consuming fish causes a severe skin disease called vitiligo (leucoderma).
content: HEALTH WARNING: Never eat ice cream or milk products after eating fish. The combination creates a chemical reaction in the body causing WHITE PATCHES on skin (vitiligo). Many dermatologists have confirmed this. Please share for awareness.

comments.content: My doctor specifically said this is a myth. Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition and has nothing to do with food combinations.

evidence.title: Dermatological research on vitiligo
evidence.description: Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition where melanocytes are destroyed by the immune system. No peer-reviewed study links it to food combinations. The Indian Association of Dermatologists has called this a myth.

title: WhatsApp forward about free COVID booster causing heart attacks
claim: The new COVID booster vaccine being given for free at government hospitals contains a substance that causes heart attacks within 6 months.
content: ⚠️ DO NOT TAKE THE NEW COVID BOOSTER! It contains graphene oxide that causes blood clots and heart attacks. 3 people in Mumbai hospital died within 6 months of taking it. Government is hiding the data. REFUSE the injection and warn your family!!! 🚫💉

comments.content: The graphene oxide claim has been debunked by multiple international health organisations including WHO. COVID vaccines do not contain graphene oxide.
The '3 deaths in Mumbai' claim has no source. Neither any hospital nor health authority has reported such deaths linked to the booster.

evidence.title: WHO fact-check on graphene oxide in vaccines
evidence.description: WHO has confirmed COVID vaccines approved for use do not contain graphene oxide. Vaccine ingredients are publicly listed by manufacturers and regulatory bodies.

title: TRAI allocates dedicated 1600-series mobile prefix for official bank calls to halt caller ID spoofing
claim: TRAI has mandated that all commercial transactional calls from banks and regulated financial institutions must originate from numbers starting with '1600'.
content: Official Circular from TRAI & RBI: Beginning late 2026, all legitimate voice calls regarding OTPs, KYC, or fraud alerts from scheduled commercial banks will use the designated '1600' series. Any regular 10-digit number claiming to be your bank is unverified.

comments.content: Verified on trai.gov.in Gazette publication dated Oct 2026. This is authentic regulatory policy.

evidence.title: TRAI Gazette Notification on 1600-series prefix allocation
evidence.description: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued directional orders to telecom service providers allocating the 1600-series numbering plan solely to RBI and SEBI regulated entities.

title: RBI & NPCI roll out interoperable QR codes connecting Digital Rupee (CBDC) with UPI
claim: Citizens can now scan any standard merchant UPI QR code across India to pay directly using their official RBI Digital Rupee (e₹) wallet.
content: RBI Press Release: In an interoperability breakthrough, NPCI has enabled standard UPI QR codes to accept Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) e₹ payments without requiring merchants to deploy separate QR codes.

comments.content: Tested on my banking CBDC app. It seamlessly scanned a merchant BharatPe UPI code and deducted e₹ tokens.

evidence.title: RBI Central Bank Digital Currency Interoperability Circular
evidence.description: The Reserve Bank of India announced that commercial bank CBDC wallet apps have integrated UPI rail interoperability.

title: Government launches Sanchar Saathi CEIR portal allowing citizens to block stolen mobile phones nationwide
claim: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) allows citizens across all Indian states to instantly block and track stolen or lost smartphones using the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR).
content: Official Announcement: Citizens who lose their mobile phone can now visit sancharsaathi.gov.in, enter their police complaint and IMEI number, to render the stolen device inoperable across all Indian telecom networks.

evidence.title: DoT Sanchar Saathi Official Portal Release
evidence.description: Department of Telecommunications confirmed CEIR has blocked over 1.4 million lost/stolen handsets across India.

title: NHAI enforces 'One Vehicle, One FASTag' policy deactivating duplicate tags at toll plazas
claim: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has phased out multiple FASTags registered to a single vehicle to streamline automated tolling.
content: Notice: Under the 'One Vehicle, One FASTag' initiative, only the latest FASTag registered to your vehicle RC will remain operational. Previous duplicate or unlinked FASTags have been blacklisted by IHMCL.

evidence.title: NHAI Official Press Release on One Vehicle One FASTag
evidence.description: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) circular mandating compliance with single tag per chassis number.

title: Indian Railways updates Advance Train Ticket Reservation Period from 120 days to 60 days
claim: Ministry of Railways notified that passenger train advance ticket bookings are revised to a 60-day window to reduce ticket hoarding and last-minute cancellations.
content: IRCTC & Indian Railways Announcement: The Advance Reservation Period (ARP) for booking train tickets is shortened from 120 days to 60 days (excluding the day of journey). Already booked tickets remain unaffected.

evidence.title: Ministry of Railways Commercial Circular on ARP Revision
evidence.description: Indian Railways gazette order reducing ARP window to 60 days with effect from the designated cutoff date.
